channel.title: Psypost – Bias and Credibility - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Psypost – Bias and Credibility (psypost.org)

item.title: New relationships take a surprising physical toll on older adults
item.description: Older adults are usually better at handling relationship friction, but a new study reveals that new dating disrupts this emotional advantage. When navigating a fresh romance, older individuals experience worse physical and emotional reactions to conflict than younger daters.

item.title: Researchers find major flaws in the historical clinical trials used to justify spanking
item.description: Proponents of physical punishment often cite historical experiments to justify the practice. However, a new analysis published in Child Abuse & Neglect suggests these older studies are deeply flawed and fail to prove spanking works.

item.title: A parent's mental health is linked to their teenager's screen time and exercise habits
item.description: Research following nearly 6,000 parent-adolescent pairs over three years found that strong parental mental well-being is tied to higher physical activity and lower digital media use in teens, highlighting the family dynamics behind healthy youth behaviors.

item.title: Brain scans reveal Democrats and Republicans use different neural pathways to buy groceries
item.description: When choosing between milk and eggs, Democrats and Republicans buy the exact same grocery items. However, a neuroimaging study shows that their brains use entirely different neural pathways to make those identical decisions.

item.title: Occasional use of classic psychedelics linked to enhanced cognitive flexibility in young adults
item.description: Sporadic recreational use of magic mushrooms and LSD does not damage memory or attention, a new study finds. Instead, young adults who occasionally use classic psychedelics display a distinct advantage in shifting problem-solving strategies and adapting to new rules.

item.title: Global experiment supports Darwin's century-old hunch about auditory aesthetics
item.description: Charles Darwin suspected that humans and animals share similar aesthetic tastes. A new citizen science experiment supports this hypothesis, showing that people strongly prefer the exact same acoustic patterns that attract female animals.

item.title: Chronic medical conditions predict childhood depression more strongly than social or family hardships
item.description: New research in the Journal of Affective Disorders provides evidence that children with chronic illnesses face a significantly higher risk of depression. This suggests a strong need to combine physical and mental healthcare for young patients.

item.title: Menstrual hormones may worsen ADHD symptoms in medicated women
item.description: New research shows that ADHD symptoms and negative moods can peak during menstruation. The findings suggest that clinicians and patients may need to account for hormonal fluctuations when planning daily tasks or designing effective prescription treatment regimens.

item.title: What brain waves reveal about people who can solve a Rubik's Cube in seconds
item.description: Scientists recently discovered that expert Rubik's Cube players show the same brain activity when planning a solution and moving the pieces. The study, published in Experimental Brain Research, indicates these experts solve the puzzle entirely in their minds.

item.title: Playing Call of Duty before bed doesn't ruin sleep, and it might even boost your memory
item.description: A recent experiment reveals that playing an action video game for an hour before bed can reduce stress and improve visuospatial memory the next day without disrupting objective sleep quality.
